thesis: Hess Midstream LP (NYSE: HESM), Bakken gathering, processing and terminaling owned partly by Chevron (96% of revenue). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read. Q3 revenue 410.1M vs 420.9M (-2.6%); 9M 1,199.2M vs 1,217.1M (-1.5%); volumes -4% to -10% on lower production, tariffs up. 9M consolidated NI 510.5M vs 516.6M; NI attributable to Class A 283.4M vs 259.6M. TTM consolidated NI 678.5M (684.6-516.6+510.5); TTM NI to Class A 376.7M; TTM OCF 1,045.4M (983.8-738.2+799.8) less capex 144.3M (255.6-188.9+77.6) = FCF 901.1M. Close 29.05 (2026-11-20, three sources agree) x Class A 128,350,881 = 3.73B (9.9x NI to Class A); counting Class B 77,827,485 (Chevron-held OpCo claims) the economic equity is 206.18M units = 5.99B = 8.8x consolidated TTM NI and FCF yield 15.0% on that basis. Debt 3,599.0M carrying (519.2M current: credit facilities due July 2027), cash 1.0M; 9M segment Adjusted EBITDA 939.2M (annualised about 1.25B, own estimate, so net debt about 2.9x). Ratings BBB- / Ba1. The valuation is NOT reliable: on 2026-10-06 HESM signed a deal with Chevron (8-K Item 1.01, read) to buy Chevron's DJ Basin gathering assets and the GP for 200M cash plus working capital, retire Chevron's Class B and Class A stake (shares down nearly 40%), but in return rewrite the Bakken commercial agreements with lower tariffs and fees (amounts not disclosed in the 8-K), a minimum revenue commitment of 80% of expected Chevron revenue to 2033, 20-year terms to 2045. Stock fell 15.5% to 32.71 on 10-07 and is 29.05 now. Pro forma EBITDA, tariff cut size and DJ asset earnings are not read, so whether 29 is cheap cannot be determined. Distributions 0.7985 per Class A share declared 10-26 (+1.2% q/q).
counterthesis: Headline multiples look low only because they ignore the signed deal that cuts Bakken tariffs paid by 96% of revenue; the size of the cut and DJ Basin EBITDA are undisclosed in the sources read, so earnings power after closing may be materially lower per share than TTM. Volumes fell 4-10% in Q3 on lower Chevron production, there is no real third-party diversification (about 4% of revenue), Moody's rates it Ba1 (sub investment grade), 519M of debt falls due July 2027, and the company becomes independent with a transition services agreement and a 2028 board election date. Buybacks and distributions (9M: 300.1M shareholders, 181.8M to noncontrolling interest, 60M repurchases) consume about 75% of 9M FCF of 722.2M.
invalidation: Downgrade to avoid if the published pro forma Adjusted EBITDA after the tariff reset falls more than about 15% below TTM, if the deal terms are amended adversely, or if Q4 volumes keep falling more than 5% with no DJ offset. Upgrade to further study only after the full purchase agreement exhibit and any investor presentation quantify tariffs, DJ EBITDA and pro forma leverage, peers (WES, KNTK, AM, ET) are compared, and the quote origins are documented.
